chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of our companions, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah created the Prophets upon prophethood, so they will not be except prophets; and He created the believers upon faith, so they will not be except believers; and He lent faith to a people. So if He wills, He completes it for them, and if He wills, He takes it away from them.
He said: And among them, it flowed, so [there are] those who are stable and those who are temporary (deposited).
And he said to me: So-and-so had temporary faith. So when he lied against us, that faith of his was taken away.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between permanent faith and temporary faith in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia doctrine of *al-Amānah* (temporary faith), distinguishing between innate, permanent faith in Prophets and true believers, and the contingent faith granted to others. It highlights the dynamic nature of belief, where faith is 'deposited' and can be revoked or confirmed based on divine decree and human actions, such as truthfulness or lying. This concept underscores the interplay between divine will (*mashī'ah*) and human agency in maintaining spiritual integrity.
